title: The efficacy of modulated whole-body electromyostimulation (WB-EMS) and nutritional therapy in patients with solid tumors of the gastrointestinal tract (excluding duodenal, liver and pancreatic carcinomas)
summary:
This study aims to combine the applicability and effectiveness of a form of strength training with targeted nutritional training. For this purpose, training with electromyostimulation (application of low frequency current) is carried out, which pursues the effect of cell activation and the improvement of muscle strength. The primary aim of the multimodal intervention presented here is to increase muscle mass and improve energy utilisation and metabolism. Patients should experience increased mobility and independence as a result of this intervention. In the study, patients are randomly assigned to one of two groups, with one group receiving an application of electricity and the other group performing standardised live-remote exercise therapy without electricity. Otherwise, the groups do not differ in the applications or tests. In addition, nutritional coaching takes place in both groups with digital nutritional coaching.  
You are a patient with a malignant tumour of the oesophagus, stomach, or colon or rectum and meet the following inclusion criteria: 1) patients after surgery without further therapy or with medical therapy administered before or after surgery (neoadjuvant and adjuvant therapy), 2) medical clearance for exercise training, 3) written informed consent from the study participant and 4) age ≥ = 18 years. 
The aim is to compare the use of electromyostimulation in this multimodal approach regarding its effectiveness in terms of muscle growth compared to the conventional multimodal approach. The research hypothesis is that the additional training stimulus provided by the application of electricity leads to significantly higher muscle growth than conventional training without electricity.
conditions: Solid tumours of the oesophagus, stomach, or colon or rectum

interventions.name: Intervention group receives multimodal therapy with whole-body electromyostimulation and exercise therapy (twice a week, lasting 11-20 minutes, over 12 weeks, 24 training sessions in total) as well as conventional nutritional counselling with guidelines and digital nutritional coaching

Control group receives multimodal therapy with moderate conventional exercise training in a group (supervised live-remote group training twice a week,  lasting 20 minutes, over 12 weeks, 24 training sessions in total) and conventional nutritional counselling with guidelines and digital nutritional c

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Patients with oesophageal, gastric, colon or rectal cancer following surgery without further therapy and with neoadjuvant and adjuvant therapy    
- medical clearance for exercise training
- written declaration of consent from the study participant
Exclusion criteria:
- Participation in another study on the topic of exercise or nutrition
- Electronic implants such as pacemakers, pumps, and coronary stents
- Cardiac arrhythmia 
- Implants in the area of application (e.g. breast implants) 
- Pregnancy 
- Epilepsy
- Wounds and open skin diseases in the area of application of the electrodes
- Unhealed operations or bone fractures
- Acute inflammatory diseases (e.g. inflammation of the intervertebral discs, bones, vessels, or soft tissue)
- Directly after herniated discs or other instabilities such as large abdominal wall hernias
- Blood clots (thromboses)
- Bone diseases with high-grade osteoporosis
- Increased risk of haemorrhage
- Fever and illnesses that can be aggravated by physical exertion
- Untreated high blood pressure
- Blindness
- Continuous parenteral nutrition 
- Metal and electronic parts in the body (e.g. prostheses, metal vascular clips, hearing aids/inner ear/cochlear implants, magnetic dental prostheses, pacemakers, contraceptives)
